findings.summary: `calls(String)`'s javadoc states "refused ones included" for EVERY verb; the position of `record` is pinned for only four of ten. MEASURED surviving: `record("putIfAbsent")` and `record("get")` moved below `refuseIfPartitioned`, 494/494 green each.
findings.detail: Round 4's named mutation is DEAD, and the new assertion is the killer: `calls++` deleted from `record` and restored as the first statement of `refuseIfPartitioned` now fails exactly one test, FaultInjectingStoreTest.theVerbsThatSKIPThePartitionCheckAreStillCOUNTED, on the new line with message [three verbs that never reach the partition check, all three in the total] expected: 3 but was: 0. Nothing incidental kills it -- the other `calls()` assertion (theMeterNamesTheVERBAndNotMerelyTheCOUNT, put+stat+stat) passes mutated, because all three of those verbs do reach the partition check. All twelve re-confirmation mutations also die (see the report). What remains is a smaller member of the same family the task exists to end. MEASURED, both surviving all 494 tests with the sweep green: (a) `record("putIfAbsent")` moved from the top of `putIfAbsent` to just below `refuseIfPartitioned()`; (b) `record("stat")`'s sibling for `get` -- `record("get")` swapped below `refuseIfPartitioned()`. Neither draws randomness, so the sweep is unchanged, and nothing asserts `calls("putIfAbsent")` or `calls("get")` anywhere in the tree. The concrete future failure: `putIfAbsent` is the CHAIN APPEND, so the first meter that credits an append -- the natural next use of the per-verb ledger -- would silently stop counting refused appends and red a floor with no defect present, which is verbatim the pre-M5.29 shape. The javadoc at :159 is what a reader takes the contract from and it claims all verbs unconditionally. ⚠️ RECOMMENDED RECORDED, NOT FIXED (review.md rule 11): M5.49's cell already enumerates what IS pinned (stat, list, putIfMatch at two positions) and adding `putIfAbsent`/`get` to that sentence is one clause, whereas two more T1 cases in a sixth round would add exactly the prose surface rule 11 warns about. It does not block; the packet's own history shows this sentence carrying a wrong count twice, so NAME the unpinned verbs rather than count them.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand gives the per-verb ledger its natural second consumer -- a meter that credits a CHAIN APPEND, `putIfAbsent`, the way this commit's meter credits `putIfMatch` -- and at the same time someone tidies `FaultInjectingStore.putIfAbsent` by moving its `record("putIfAbsent")` below `refuseIfPartitioned()`, which reads as harmless because `record` draws no randomness and the sweep totals do not move. MEASURED: that move survives all 494 tests today. Refused appends then stop being counted, the new floor reds on a tree with no defect in it, and `calls(String)`'s javadoc at :159 -- which says "refused ones included" without qualification -- tells the person debugging it that the counter is right. That is the pre-M5.29 failure shape (a floor redding with no bug present) reintroduced at a verb the commit did not pin, and the same move on `get` survives identically.
